newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq slips for 2nd straight session.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq slips for 2nd straight session.

text.p: Nasdaq stocks fell for the second straight session on Wednesday, with traders scrambling to lock in profits after bullish data on semiconductors.
The Nasdaq Composite fell 2.17 to 1237.98, with losers outpacing winners by a margin of about 11 to eight. The broader Russell 2000 dropped 1.26 to 346.10.

"Book to bill was the big thing today," said Patrick Davis, head of OTC trading at Salomon Brothers. "It was viewed favorably, but you have to remember that the positive was already in the price of stocks." On Tuesday, the book-to-bill ratio was reported at 0.99 for September, up from a revised 0.93 in August.
Davis said much of the session was dominated by traditional profit taking. "We've had a pretty good scoot here for a long time," he said.
Intel led the most actives, with shares off 3/4 to 100-7/8 on volume of about 13 million shares. The stock hit an closing high of 104-3/4 on Monday.
Pairgain Technology lost 6-1/2 to 73-1/4 after First Boston downgraded the stock. One analyst said the share drop was due to profit taking.
Tellabs rose six to 79 after announcing earnings on Tuesday that exceeded Wall Street estimates.
